messages:
Mike R.: quick heads-up — I ran a microbench comparing our new layer-aware quant plan vs the baseline. seeing ~9% throughput drop on 4-bit path for long sequences when embeddings are excluded, but perplexity unchanged on our quick eval set. logs below.

Sophia L.: can you paste the exact commands / profile output? also which kernels were chosen?

Mike R.: sure. run command:```./tools/bench_infer --model gptx-small --seq 1024 --batch 8 --quant profile --config configs/layer_aware_exclude_emb.json```profile excerpt:```kernel: int4-gemm-v1  time_per_token: 1.24ms  kv-touch: high  fallback_rate: 0.0
kernel: fp8-attn-opt  time_per_token: 0.48ms  kv-touch: low
end-to-end throughput: 720 tok/s (baseline 793 tok/s)
````

Jordan P.: hmm 9% seems significant. could be the batching heuristic interacting with KV cache warmup. are we forcing continuous batching for the quant trace?

Mike R.: we enabled continous-batcher v3 (adaptive latency SLO=80ms). interestingly the perf drop mainly shows up after 150 tokens — warmup period. before that, int4 path is on par.

Sophia L.: that hints at KV cache eviction or per-layer kernel mismatch as sequence grows. do we have kernel selection logs? which layers switched to fp8 mid-seq?

Mike R.: yes — selection log shows middle layers 9-18 switching to fp8 kernels on long sequences due to a heuristic that avoids int4 for high activation variance. example: "layer_12: selected fp8-attn-opt due to act_std>0.23"

Anya (perf-bot): automation note: flagged run 1764120000 as regression candidate. diff vs baseline: -9.2% throughput, +0.0% ppl, CPU jitter +2%.

Jordan P.: two hypotheses: 1) the selection heuristic oscillates across iterations causing kernel churn and extra kernel reconfig costs; 2) longer sequences push more KV buffer swaps (slab allocs) when using int4 kernels with our current KV layout.

Sophia L.: agree. for hypothesis 1 can we add hysteresis to kernel selector: require 2 consecutive windows before switching, and measure overhead of rebind. for hypothesis 2, try switching KV layout to sticky-slab for int4 and re-run.

Mike R.: I'll try both in parallel. quick patch for selector: add "min_confirm_windows=2" to selector config. KV change: set kv.alloc_strategy=sticky-slab. will push PR and run same bench.

Deploy Bot: mike-r pushed branch "layer-quant-hysteresis" to staging (CI queue #112).

Mike R.: test1 (hysteresis only): throughput -> 787 tok/s (baseline 793), rebind count dropped from 7->1 per request, warmup tail reduced.

Mike R.: test2 (sticky-slab only): throughput -> 762 tok/s, kv alloc churn down, but per-token kernel time still slightly higher.

Sophia L.: interesting — hysteresis recovered most of the loss. suggests kernel churn was the main culprit. can you also capture kernel switch latency (ms) and memcpy counts?

Mike R.: yes — kernel switch latency was ~12ms per switch, memcpy spikes aligned with switches. with hysteresis we eliminated 6 switches -> saved ~72ms per warmup.

Jordan P.: great find. next steps: 1) keep hysteresis by default for mixed precision selection, 2) add metric to console for kernel-switch-count, 3) evaluate end-to-end latency SLO for realistic traffic (varying seq len).

Sophia L.: also add a small experiment: try excluding lm_head from quant (we excluded embeddings already). that sometimes moves compute to fp8 only at output and helps numeric stability.

Mike R.: noted. I'll run lm_head-excluded + hysteresis + sticky-slab and report. TL;DR: don't ship plan that toggles kernels mid-request. :+1:

Anya (perf-bot): follow-up scheduled: perf-bisect job created (job id 1764120000-bisect).
